{{Short description|American physicist and science writer}}
{{Infobox writer|birth_date=1937|subject=[[physics]]|notable_works=''Thinking Physics''}}
'''Lewis Carroll Epstein''' is the author of layman's books on [[physics]] that use an idiosyncratic mix of cartoons and single-page brain teasers to pull the reader into advanced concepts in [[classical mechanics]], [[Quantum mechanics|quantum theory]], and [[Theory of relativity|relativity]].<ref name="OpenLibrary0">{{Cite book |date=2025-04-21 |title=Open Library description for "Thinking physics is Gedanken Physics" (ol = 18198258M) | ol=18198258M }}</ref><ref name="Amazon">{{Cite book |last1=Epstein |first1=Lewis C. |title=Amazon.com Editorial product description for "Thinking Physics: Understandable Practical Reality" |year=2002 |publisher=Insight Press |isbn=0935218084 |edition=3rd}}</ref>

His books ''Thinking Physics'' and ''Thinking Physics is Gedanken Physics'' have been republished for almost 30 years, the former being on the [[Exploratorium]] recommended science reading list.<ref name="OpenLibrary1">{{Cite web |date=2009-12-10 |title=Open Library republication dates for Thinking Physics (ol = 8712446W) |url=https://openlibrary.org/works/OL8712446W/Thinking_physics?edition=key%3A/books/OL21382430M |website=Thinking physics}}</ref><ref name="OpenLibrary2">{{Cite web |title=Open Library republication dates for Thinking Physics is Gedanken Physics (ol = 5921987W) |url=https://openlibrary.org/works/OL5921987W/Thinking_physics_is_Gedanken_physics |website=[[Open Library]]}}</ref><ref name="Exploratorium">{{Cite web |date=2015-02-25 |title=Exploratorium reading list |url=http://www.exploratorium.edu/snacks/snacksupplies.html|website=Exploratorium.edu}}</ref>  He credits his teaching style to experience presenting technical testimony to trial juries and congressional hearings.<ref>Epstein, Lewis, Thinking Physics is Gedanken Physics, {{ISBN|0-935218-06-8}}</ref>
